name: VirusTotal Domain
description: Check a domain against 80+ antivirus engines and threat intelligence sources.
whyUse: Aggregates reputation data from dozens of vendors in one place. Fast first pivot for any domain.
lookFor: Detection ratio, community scores, passive DNS history, WHOIS, subdomains, related files.
riskNote: Submitting a domain will be logged by VirusTotal. Avoid submitting sensitive internal domains.

name: VirusTotal IP
description: Check an IP address against VirusTotal's threat intel aggregator.
whyUse: Quick reputation check for IPs. Shows detections, passive DNS, communicating files, and community notes.
lookFor: Detection flags, associated domains, communicating samples, last seen timestamps.
riskNote: IP lookups are logged. Do not use for sensitive internal IPs.

name: VirusTotal File Hash
description: Look up a file hash (MD5, SHA1, SHA256) in VirusTotal to check for known malware.
whyUse: Fastest way to check if a file is known malicious. Covers 80+ AV engines.
lookFor: Detection ratio, engine names, file type, first/last seen, behaviour reports if available.
riskNote: Hash lookups are logged by VirusTotal. The hash itself is low-risk to submit but confirms you have the file.

name: urlscan.io Search
description: Search urlscan.io for historical scans of a domain or URL.
whyUse: Shows historical screenshots, DOM snapshots, and network activity for previous scans of a site. Excellent for phishing triage.
lookFor: Page screenshots, external resource loads, certificates, IP resolutions, phishing indicators.
riskNote: Searching is low risk. Submitting a new scan will take a live screenshot — do not submit sensitive URLs.

name: GreyNoise IP
description: Check if an IP is known internet background noise (scanners, crawlers, mass exploit attempts).
whyUse: Differentiates targeted attacks from mass internet noise. Reduces false positives for WAF and firewall alerts.
lookFor: Classification (noise/riot/malicious), tags (Mirai, scanner, Tor, etc.), first/last seen, ASN.
riskNote: IP lookup only. Low risk.

name: AbuseIPDB
description: Community-driven IP abuse reporting database. Check and report malicious IPs.
whyUse: Shows community abuse reports for an IP including categories (brute force, port scan, spam, etc.).
lookFor: Abuse confidence score, number of reports, categories, last reported date, ISP.
riskNote: Lookup only. Reporting an IP makes it public.

name: IPinfo
description: Detailed IP geolocation, ASN, and hosting provider information.
whyUse: Quickly identify the owning ASN, hosting provider, and geographic location of an IP.
lookFor: ASN, organisation, city/country, hosting vs residential, abuse contact.
riskNote: Lookup only. Low risk.

name: IPVoid
description: Multi-source IP blacklist check across many threat feeds.
whyUse: Aggregates many blacklists in one check. Useful when you want breadth of coverage.
lookFor: Number of blacklists flagging the IP, which specific lists, detection ratio.
riskNote: Navigate to the site and enter IP manually. Template links to the tool homepage.

name: URLVoid
description: Multi-source domain/URL blacklist check.
whyUse: Aggregates domain reputation across multiple threat feeds and blacklists.
lookFor: Detection count, which blacklists flagged it, WHOIS data, IP address.
riskNote: Submits domain to scan. Avoid internal domain names.

name: Talos Reputation Center
description: Cisco Talos reputation lookup for IPs, domains, and URLs.
whyUse: Cisco Talos has broad visibility from email gateways, firewalls, and endpoint products. Strong for spam and email threat context.
lookFor: Reputation score, email volume history, threat category, Sender Base score.
riskNote: Lookup only. Low risk.

name: FortiGuard Web Filter
description: FortiGuard URL and domain categorisation lookup.
whyUse: Check how FortiGuard categorises a domain. Useful if your org uses FortiGate and you need to understand why traffic was blocked or allowed.
lookFor: Category assigned, risk level, FortiGuard recommendation.
riskNote: Lookup only. Low risk.

name: BrightCloud URL/IP Lookup
description: BrightCloud (Webroot) reputation and categorisation lookup.
whyUse: Webroot-powered reputation. Useful for cross-referencing if Webroot products are in your environment.
lookFor: Reputation score, category, first seen date.
riskNote: Navigate and enter manually. Template links to tool homepage.

name: AlienVault OTX
description: Open Threat Exchange — community threat intelligence pulses for IPs, domains, hashes, and more.
whyUse: Broad community-sourced threat intel. Check for associated malware campaigns, threat actor attribution, and related indicators.
lookFor: Pulse count, threat actor tags, related indicators, MITRE ATT&CK techniques.
riskNote: Lookup only. Low risk.

name: IBM X-Force Exchange
description: IBM X-Force threat intelligence platform for IPs, URLs, hashes, and vulnerabilities.
whyUse: IBM's commercial threat feed. Good cross-reference especially for enterprise environments.
lookFor: Risk score, categories, associated reports, malware families.
riskNote: Lookup only. Some features require account.

name: DNSDumpster
description: Free DNS recon tool. Shows DNS records, subdomains, and related hosts.
whyUse: Quickly enumerate a domain's DNS posture — useful for understanding attack surface or verifying legitimate infrastructure.
lookFor: MX records, A/AAAA records, subdomains, hosting providers, related IPs.
riskNote: Enter domain manually on the site. Template links to the tool homepage.

name: crt.sh Certificate Search
description: Search Certificate Transparency logs for domains and subdomains.
whyUse: Certificate Transparency logs reveal all SSL certificates ever issued for a domain, including subdomains. Essential for attack surface mapping.
lookFor: Subdomains, certificate issue dates, certificate authority, wildcard certs.
riskNote: Lookup only. Public CT log data — no sensitivity.

name: Shodan Host
description: View open ports, services, and banners for a specific IP address.
whyUse: Shows what services are exposed on an IP. Useful for confirming if a server is a known scanner, VPN node, or exposed service.
lookFor: Open ports, service banners, SSL certificates, known vulnerabilities (CVEs), hostnames.
riskNote: Lookup only. Shodan may have indexed your assets — no additional exposure from searching.

name: Shodan Search
description: Search Shodan for domains, hostnames, and internet-exposed assets.
whyUse: Search Shodan for services associated with a domain name. Reveals hosting, infrastructure, and exposed assets.
lookFor: Servers hosting the domain, exposed services, cloud providers, unusual ports.
riskNote: Lookup only.

name: Censys Host
description: Censys host-level view of open ports, services, and certificates for an IP.
whyUse: Similar to Shodan. Good for cross-referencing open ports and certificates on an IP.
lookFor: Open ports, TLS certificates, ASN, hostnames, services.
riskNote: Lookup only.

name: Censys Search
description: Search Censys for domains, certificates, and internet-facing assets.
whyUse: Useful for finding all IPs hosting a domain or certificate. Good for external attack surface enumeration.
lookFor: Hosts, certificates, exposed services linked to the domain.
riskNote: Lookup only.

name: WhoisXML API
description: WHOIS lookup for domain registration details.
whyUse: Check domain registration dates, registrar, registrant details, and nameservers. Useful for takedowns and phishing investigations.
lookFor: Registration date (newly registered = suspicious), registrar, privacy shield, nameservers, registrant contact.
riskNote: Navigate to the site. Template links to the lookup page. Enter domain manually.

name: DomainTools WHOIS
description: DomainTools WHOIS lookup with historical registration data.
whyUse: DomainTools has historical WHOIS and domain registration pivots. Useful for tracking domain infrastructure changes over time.
lookFor: Registration history, related domains by registrant, nameserver changes, registrar.
riskNote: Lookup only. Full pivots require paid account.

name: CyberChef
description: Browser-based data transformation and decoding tool from GCHQ.
whyUse: Decode base64, URL encoding, XOR, hash, and many other transformations. Runs entirely in your browser — no data leaves your machine.
lookFor: Decoded payloads, obfuscated URLs, encoded commands, base64 blobs.
riskNote: Runs locally in your browser. No data is sent to any server. Safe for sensitive data.

name: Unfurl
description: Visual URL decomposer — breaks URLs into their component parts for forensic analysis.
whyUse: Visually decodes URL structures including base64 parameters, timestamps, and tracking tokens. Runs in browser.
lookFor: Hidden parameters, tracking IDs, encoded values, structural anomalies.
riskNote: Runs in your browser. Low risk if you paste URL into the local tool rather than submitting to external API.

name: PhishTool
description: Email and phishing triage platform. Analyse email headers and URLs.
whyUse: Purpose-built for phishing triage. Parses email headers, analyses URLs, and provides contextualised threat intel.
lookFor: Header anomalies, SPF/DKIM/DMARC results, URL analysis, threat classification.
riskNote: Uploading email samples sends data to PhishTool. Check your data handling policy.

name: URLhaus
description: Abuse.ch database of malware distribution URLs.
whyUse: Check if a URL or domain has been reported as a malware distribution point.
lookFor: Malware type, associated tags, status (online/offline), date added, payloads.
riskNote: Lookup only. Low risk.

name: ThreatFox
description: Abuse.ch IOC sharing platform for malware C2s, URLs, and hashes.
whyUse: Check if an IOC is a known malware C2 or has been associated with a threat actor.
lookFor: Malware family, threat actor, confidence level, first/last seen, related IOCs.
riskNote: Lookup only. Low risk.

name: ANY.RUN Intelligence
description: ANY.RUN threat intelligence portal. Search for IOC associations, malware families, and threat actor infrastructure.
whyUse: Search for malware family associations, threat actor infrastructure, network indicators, and related IOCs from sandbox telemetry.
lookFor: Malware family classifications, associated C2 domains/IPs, threat actor clusters, related samples.
riskNote: Lookup only against existing intelligence. Low risk.

name: ANY.RUN Sandbox
description: Interactive online malware sandbox. Search for existing reports or submit samples for dynamic analysis.
whyUse: Run or find interactive sandbox reports with live process trees, network capture, and behaviour classification.
lookFor: Process tree, network connections (DNS, HTTP, C2), dropped files, registry changes, MITRE ATT&CK mapping.
riskNote: Submitting a new sample makes it public on the free tier. Searching existing reports is lower risk. Check your SOC policy before submitting.

name: Lookyloo
description: Web page capture and analysis tool. Takes a full browser rendering of a URL.
whyUse: Captures full page renders with resource loads, redirects, and DOM screenshots. Good for phishing and takedown evidence.
lookFor: Redirect chains, credential harvesting forms, external resource loads, final rendered page.
riskNote: Lookyloo makes an active request to the target URL. Do not use for sensitive or internal URLs. The capture may be public.

name: phish.report
description: Submit phishing URLs for takedown via phish.report's automated reporting pipeline.
whyUse: Streamlines phishing takedown requests by submitting to hosting providers, registrars, and abuse contacts.
lookFor: Abuse contact found, takedown timeline, report confirmation.
riskNote: Submitting a URL triggers active takedown requests. Confirm the URL is malicious before submitting.

name: Google Safe Browsing Report Phish
description: Report a phishing URL to Google Safe Browsing for protective blacklisting.
whyUse: Reporting to Google Safe Browsing gets the URL flagged in Chrome, Firefox, and other browsers that use GSB.
lookFor: Confirmation of report submission.
riskNote: Submitting reports the URL to Google. Do not submit internal or false-positive URLs.

name: SynapsInt
description: Unified OSINT platform for domains, IPs, emails, and certificates.
whyUse: Aggregates multiple OSINT sources into a single interface. Good for rapid domain/IP pivoting.
lookFor: Associated domains, IP infrastructure, certificates, social media presence.
riskNote: Enter IOC manually on the site. Template links to homepage.

name: Intelligence X
description: Search engine for dark web, data leaks, and OSINT across many sources.
whyUse: Searches dark web forums, Telegram, paste sites, and data breach archives for mentions of an IOC.
lookFor: Credential leaks, mentions in breach data, dark web discussions, paste site exposures.
riskNote: Navigate and search manually. Some features require paid tier.

name: WhiteIntel
description: Platform for monitoring dark web credential exposure and stealer logs.
whyUse: Monitors stealer malware logs for compromised credentials associated with your domain or email addresses.
lookFor: Stolen credentials, session tokens from infostealers, affected usernames.
riskNote: Navigate to the platform. Registration required.

name: IPQualityScore
description: IP reputation, proxy/VPN/Tor detection, and fraud scoring.
whyUse: Detects VPNs, proxies, Tor exit nodes, and residential proxies. Strong fraud scoring.
lookFor: Proxy/VPN/Tor flag, fraud score, ISP, connection type, abuse history.
riskNote: Lookup only. Low risk.

name: Spur
description: Specialised IP proxy and VPN intelligence. Identifies residential proxies, VPN exits, and anonymisation infrastructure.
whyUse: Spur has deep intelligence on proxy networks, residential proxies, and anonymisation services. Useful for identifying bypass attempts.
lookFor: Proxy type, network infrastructure, associated users (anonymised), confidence score.
riskNote: Lookup only. Some detail requires paid tier.

name: IP Teoh VPN Detection
description: Quick VPN and proxy detection for IP addresses.
whyUse: Lightweight VPN/proxy check. Fast to use for a quick second opinion.
lookFor: VPN detected flag, provider name, risk level.
riskNote: Lookup only. Low risk.

name: urlquery.net
description: URL scanning and analysis service. Checks for malicious content and drive-by downloads.
whyUse: Scans URLs for malicious scripts, exploit kits, and suspicious redirects.
lookFor: IDS alerts, JavaScript anomalies, redirect chains, external resource loads.
riskNote: Submitting a URL triggers a live scan. Do not submit sensitive or internal URLs.

name: WannaBrowser
description: Headless browser URL analysis. Visit URLs safely to see what they serve.
whyUse: Browse suspicious URLs in a sandboxed browser without exposing your workstation. Good for quick visual analysis.
lookFor: Page content, redirects, credentials harvesting forms, malicious scripts.
riskNote: WannaBrowser makes an active request to the target URL. Do not use for internal URLs.

name: Ransomware.live
description: Live tracking of ransomware groups, victims, and campaigns.
whyUse: Check if a domain or organisation has appeared in ransomware group leak sites. Useful for dark web exposure assessment.
lookFor: Victim listings, ransomware group attribution, leak dates, data types exposed.
riskNote: Lookup only. Navigate manually.

name: MXToolbox
description: Email deliverability and DNS diagnostics. SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MX record lookup and blacklist check.
whyUse: Verify email authentication records (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and check if a domain or IP is on email blacklists.
lookFor: SPF/DKIM/DMARC pass/fail, blacklist hits, MX record configuration issues.
riskNote: Lookup only. Low risk.

name: MalwareBazaar
description: Abuse.ch malware sample database. Search and download samples by hash, tag, or malware family.
whyUse: Check if a hash is a known malware sample. Provides file metadata, signatures, and download of the sample.
lookFor: Malware family, file type, first seen, tags, associated YARA/ClamAV rules.
riskNote: Lookup only. Downloading samples is only advisable in a secure malware analysis environment.

name: Hybrid Analysis
description: Free malware analysis sandbox with static and dynamic analysis reports.
whyUse: Search historical sandbox reports or submit a sample for analysis. Good for behavioural analysis and C2 extraction.
lookFor: Process tree, network connections, dropped files, classification verdict, MITRE ATT&CK mapping.
riskNote: Submitting a new sample makes it public. Searching existing reports is low risk.

name: Microsoft Message Header Analyzer
description: Paste raw email headers to parse and analyse routing, delays, and authentication results.
whyUse: Parses complex email headers into a readable format. Shows hop-by-hop routing, SPF/DKIM/DMARC results, and delivery delays.
lookFor: SPF/DKIM/DMARC failures, unusual relay hops, unexpected sending IPs, X-headers from security gateways.
riskNote: Runs in your browser. Email headers are processed client-side. Low risk, but avoid submitting full email bodies.

name: Hurricane Electric BGP
description: IP WHOIS, ASN, BGP routing, and peer information from Hurricane Electric.
whyUse: Single view of IP WHOIS from all RIRs alongside ASN, BGP prefixes, and upstream peers. Useful for attributing IPs to hosting providers, ISPs, or known malicious ASNs.
lookFor: RIR WHOIS data, owning organisation, ASN, BGP prefix, upstream peers, abuse contact.
riskNote: Lookup only. Low risk.

name: SecurityTrails IP History
description: Historical DNS lookup — shows all domains that have resolved to this IP address over time.
whyUse: Reveals what domains have historically pointed to an IP. Useful for identifying shared hosting, bulletproof infrastructure, or domain rotation patterns.
lookFor: Domains currently or previously resolving to the IP, hosting clusters, suspicious domain patterns, co-hosted malicious sites.
riskNote: Lookup only. Free account required for full results.

name: SANS Internet Storm Center
description: SANS ISC IP reputation feed. Shows if an IP has been reported via their global sensor and honeypot network.
whyUse: SANS ISC aggregates reports from security practitioners globally. An IP appearing here indicates observed malicious activity reported by the community.
lookFor: Report count, attack type, first/last seen, number of sources reporting, threat category.
riskNote: Lookup only. Low risk.

name: Hunter.io
description: Identify the company behind a domain. Returns organisation name, industry, employee count, email format pattern, and HQ location.
whyUse: Quickly determine if a domain belongs to a real, identifiable business. No company match is a red flag for lookalike/phishing domains.
lookFor: Organisation name (null = unregistered), email pattern, headcount, industry, city/country. Check if it's a disposable or webmail provider.
riskNote: Lookup only. Domain is sent to Hunter.io.

name: OpenCorporates
description: The world's largest open database of companies. Search by company name or domain to find registration details across 140+ jurisdictions.
whyUse: Verify that a company claiming to own a domain is actually registered. Useful for vendor vetting and supply-chain investigations.
lookFor: Company registration number, jurisdiction, registered address, directors, company status (active/dissolved), incorporation date.
riskNote: Search query sent to OpenCorporates.

name: Companies House (UK)
description: UK government register of companies. Official source for UK company registration, directors, filings, and accounts.
whyUse: Authoritative UK company verification. For incidents involving UK-based entities, this is the ground truth for company legitimacy.
lookFor: Company number, registered address, director names, filing history, company status, SIC code (business type).
riskNote: Search query sent to Companies House.

name: Whoxy WHOIS History
description: Historical WHOIS lookup service. Shows how registrant information has changed over time — previously registered to, registrar changes, ownership transfers.
whyUse: Exposes domain ownership history that current WHOIS hides. Useful for detecting re-registered domains and ownership changes that coincide with suspicious activity.
lookFor: Previous registrant names/emails, registrar history, when privacy protection was added, changes around key dates.
riskNote: Domain sent to Whoxy.

name: Wayback Machine
description: Internet Archive snapshots of web pages over time. Reveals what a domain looked like months or years ago.
whyUse: Determine how long a domain has been active and what it was used for previously. A phishing domain typically has zero or very recent snapshots.
lookFor: First snapshot date (old = more established), content at key dates, whether the domain was previously legitimate and has been taken over.
riskNote: Domain sent to archive.org.

name: BuiltWith
description: Technology profiler that shows what software, frameworks, CDNs, analytics, and hosting services a domain uses.
whyUse: A legitimate business typically runs recognisable commercial software. A phishing domain often uses minimal infrastructure. Tech stack consistency with claimed identity is a legitimacy signal.
lookFor: CMS/ecommerce platform (does it match the business type?), CDN provider, analytics tools, payment providers, hosting location.
riskNote: Domain sent to BuiltWith.

name: SecurityTrails
description: DNS history, subdomain discovery, and WHOIS history for domains. Shows historical A records, nameserver changes, and subdomains.
whyUse: Reveals historical IP addresses the domain has pointed to, subdomain infrastructure, and nameserver changes that may indicate takeovers or migration.
lookFor: Historical A records (which IPs it pointed to), nameserver changes, MX record history, subdomain list, when records changed.
riskNote: Domain sent to SecurityTrails.

name: LinkedIn Company Search
description: Search LinkedIn for a company by domain name to verify size, industry, location, and employee presence.
whyUse: A legitimate company typically has a LinkedIn presence. No presence, or a very recently created page, is a red flag.
lookFor: Company page age, employee count, industry, headquarters, whether employees are visible, company description consistency.
riskNote: Search terms sent to LinkedIn.

name: Crunchbase
description: Business information platform covering startup funding, founders, investors, and company profiles.
whyUse: Useful for verifying tech/startup companies. A missing Crunchbase profile for a claimed VC-backed or tech company is suspicious.
lookFor: Founded date, funding rounds, investor names, employee count, description, whether the domain on file matches.
riskNote: Search query sent to Crunchbase.

name: DNSDumpster
description: Free domain research tool that discovers hosts related to a domain via DNS enumeration.
whyUse: Quickly maps the DNS attack surface of a domain. Reveals mail servers, name servers, and subdomains that may expose sensitive infrastructure.
lookFor: Mail servers (MX), name servers, A records for subdomains, TXT records (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), geolocation of hosts.
riskNote: Manual search required — no URL template. Enter the domain on the site.

name: ICANN WHOIS
description: ICANN's official WHOIS and RDAP lookup. Authoritative registration data for gTLDs directly from the registry.
whyUse: When third-party WHOIS services show redacted data, ICANN's RDAP endpoint often provides more structured registrar and registration information.
lookFor: Registrar name, registration/expiry dates, nameservers, RDAP status flags, abuse contact.
riskNote: Domain sent to ICANN.

name: LeakIX
description: Indexes exposed services, leaked databases, and misconfigurations. Search by domain or organisation to find public exposure.
whyUse: Shows if a domain or organisation has publicly exposed sensitive services, databases, or misconfigurations that could indicate a breach or attract attackers.
lookFor: Exposed databases, S3 buckets, cloud storage, configuration files, leaked credentials, git repos.
riskNote: Domain sent to LeakIX.

name: Shodan Org Search
description: Search Shodan by organisation name to map the entire internet-facing infrastructure of a business.
whyUse: Gives a complete picture of what an organisation exposes to the internet. Useful for vendor risk assessment and attacker-perspective reconnaissance.
lookFor: All internet-facing IPs and ports, exposed management interfaces, default credentials, open databases, certificate mismatches.
riskNote: Query sent to Shodan. Organisation name derived from domain.
